items.title: O mundo nunca foi um lugar bom e o homem jamais foi um animal feliz

items.summary: A expressão "homem ocidental" é usada, normalmente, para designar quem vive na região ocidental em sentido geopolítico e cultural, e não geográfico. Por exemplo, o Brasil é ocidente geográfico, mas nunca é descrito como parte do ocidente geopolítico ou cultural. Por outro lado, a Austrália não é ocidente geográfico, mas é ocidente geopolítico e cultural. França, Reino Unido, Alemanha, EUA, entre outros, são exemplos desse Ocidente geopolítico e cultural. items.summary: At 102 years old, William Lyford received France's prestigious Legion of Honor, honoring his bravery during World War II, particularly his role in liberating Dachau concentration camp in 1945. The touching ceremony held in Woodstock was filled with family, friends, and fellow veterans celebrating his significant contributions. Despite his service, Lyford’s daughter shared how he rarely discussed his military past, showcasing the lasting bond between the U.S. and France.

items.title: Debt, dues and deja vu: How poor nations end up paying more than they borrow

items.summary: In 2025, low and middle-income countries are grappling with an alarming spike in external debt, hitting a staggering $9.4 trillion. Alongside this, debt repayment burdens surged to $1.4 trillion, largely due to escalating borrowing rates and a scarcity of new financial support. Nations receiving IDA funding are particularly strained, facing average interest rates of 8.2 percent.

items.title: Police secure miniature camera in tax accountant exam cheating probe
items.title_zh: 警方在税务会计师考试作弊调查中缴获微型摄像头
items.summary: Police have secured a miniature camera allegedly used by a man to cheat on this year's certified tax accountant exam and receive top marks, officials said Monday. The man admitted Sunday to cheating using generative artificial intelligence (AI), with his lawyer submitting the camera, a laptop and a mobile phone allegedly used in the scheme as evidence to police. The suspect, who scored a near perfect score in the first round of the exam, made the admission after facing scrutiny over what many saw as unrealistically high scores. Police said they plan to inspect the submitted devices to determine whether they were actually used and bring the suspect in for questioning. The devices reportedly did not include miniature earphones or AI glasses. The cheating scandal has raised concerns about possible cheating using hidden AI-assisted devices during this year's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), scheduled for Thursday. items.title: Ex-deputy national security adviser takes office as KOICA chief
items.title_zh: 前国家安全副顾问就任韩国国际协力团团长
items.summary: Oh Hyun-joo, a career diplomat who previously served as a deputy director at the presidential National Security Office, took office Monday as the 15th president of the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), the state-run foreign aid agency. KOICA is Korea’s main agency for carrying out the government’s grant aid programs for developing countries. It was founded in 1991. An inauguration ceremony was held the same day at its headquarters in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province. Oh graduated from Korea University with a degree in Spanish language and literature and earned a master’s degree in international relations from the University of Cambridge. She joined the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in 1994 after passing the foreign service exam. Her key posts include director of the ministry’s development cooperation division, counselor at Korea’s mission in Geneva, special adviser to the president of the United Nations Human Rights Council, director general for development cooperation and deputy ambassador to the U.N. In 2023, she became Korea’s first female ambassador to the Vatican.

items.summary: Namdaemun Market accessories and local food specialties are heading to smartphone screens as Seoul's Jung District is set to host a live commerce broadcast on Naver Shopping Live on Wednesday, connecting small business merchants with nationwide online shoppers. The district office announced that six merchants across five local commercial hubs — including Namdaemun Market, Jungbu Market, Shin Jungbu Market, Shin Jungang Market and Donghwa-dong Alley Shopping District — will participate in the day-long event. Four merchants will offer food items, including artisanal sesame and perilla oils from Donghwa-dong, dried seaweed from Jungbu Market, nuts and dried seafood from Shin Jungbu Market and traditional sweet puffed wheat snacks from Shin Jungang Market. Meanwhile, two vendors from Namdaemun Market will showcase fashion accessories. Running from 11 a.m. to 4:20 p.m., each store will host a dedicated 40-minute segment featuring professional show hosts. items.title: Students unveil AI tools to solve social challenges
items.title_zh: 学生们展示了用于解决社会挑战的AI工具
items.summary: Ten teams of undergraduate and graduate students showcased six months of social innovation projects in Seoul last week, presenting solutions ranging from artificial intelligence tools that ease special education teachers' workloads to an app helping visually impaired pedestrians cross streets safely. Hosted by the Seoul Future Talent Foundation at its community center, the 2026 Seoul Impact Project showcase highlighted student-led initiatives tackling persistent social challenges. After evaluating presentations, a judging panel awarded 15 million won ($10,800) in combined prize money to three standout teams. Aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, the program supports teams of two to five students creating public value. Selected through a three-stage screening process, each of the 10 teams received 5 million won in project funding and 2 million won per member in activity stipends, alongside specialized workshops. items.title: PM pledges to bring home remains of every single independence fighter from overseas
items.title_zh: 总理承诺将每一位海外独立战士的遗骸带回祖国
items.summary: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook renewed the government's commitment Monday to bringing the remains of independence fighters back home from overseas as she marked the return of the remains of two patriots who fought for Korea's independence from Japan's 1910-45 colonial rule. The remains of Ho Si-han and Lee Gwal arrived Sunday from the United States and Uzbekistan, respectively, and the government held an official ceremony at Seodaemun Independence Park in central Seoul on Monday to commemorate their return. The remains will be buried at the national cemetery in the central city of Daejeon. "I offer my infinite respect to the two patriots who, with indomitable courage and spirit, forged ahead through a treacherous, thorn-strewn path for the sake of our nation's independence," Han said. "The government will uphold the noble spirit of patriotic martyrs, with a firm commitment never to forget a single hero." items.title: Major crimes unit's Seoul office raids restaurant franchisor in 1st search operation
items.title_zh: 重案组首尔办事处在首次搜查行动中突击搜查餐厅加盟商
items.summary: The Seoul Regional Office of the Serious Crime Investigation Agency (SCIA) raided the restaurant franchisor Myeong Ryun Dang Co. on Monday over allegations of unfair affiliate support, marking its first search and seizure operation since its establishment last month. SCIA investigators began searching 26 locations, including the company's headquarters in Seoul's southern district of Songpa and the residence of company Chairman Lee Jong-geun, at around 9 a.m. Myeong Ryun Dang, the operator of the Myeongryun Jinsa Galbi barbecue restaurant franchise with stores at home and abroad, is accused of providing unfair financial support to 14 lending companies owned by Lee by extending loans totaling 298.3 billion won (US$223 million) at annual interest rates of between 2.3 percent and 4.6 percent over a period of more than four years starting in late 2021. items.title: Supreme Court to rule on ex-first lady's corruption case Thursday
items.title_zh: 最高法院将于周四对前第一夫人的腐败案作出裁决
items.summary: The Supreme Court said Monday it will deliver its verdict this week on charges that former first lady Kim Keon Hee was involved in a stock price manipulation scheme, among other offenses. The sentencing hearing has been scheduled for 4 p.m. Thursday, with the case also involving charges that former President Yoon Suk Yeol's wife accepted luxury gifts from the Unification Church and received free opinion poll results from a self-proclaimed power broker. An appellate court sentenced Kim to four years in prison and a fine of 50 million won ($37,500) after convicting her of the stock manipulation and luxury gift charges. She was acquitted of the opinion poll charge. The Supreme Court had initially planned to deliver its verdict in July, but postponed the ruling after a district court convicted Yoon of the same opinion poll charge, and referred Kim's case to its full bench. Yoon, who has also been standing multiple trials, will receive the Supreme Court's verdict on a perjury case later this month. items.title: Seoul rolls out comprehensive transit measures for college entrance exam takers
items.title_zh: 首尔为高考考生推出全面的交通出行措施
items.summary: Seoul will add subway runs, adjust bus schedules and offer free emergency rides to help students reach their test sites on time for Thursday’s College Scholastic Ability Test, the city government said. The annual exam is the main standardized test used for university admissions in Korea. This year, 113,454 students will take the exam at 228 sites in Seoul. They must enter their test sites between 6:30 a.m. and 8:10 a.m. To ease morning traffic, the workday at the city government, district offices and other public institutions will start one hour later than usual, at 10 a.m. Subways will make 27 extra runs between 6 a.m. and 10 a.m., and 15 trains will be kept on standby in case of breakdowns. City and village buses will run at their shortest intervals from 6 a.m. to 8:10 a.m. and again from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m., when students head home. The total number of daily bus runs will stay the same, so buses may come slightly less often at other times. items.title: Seoul battery tests reveal heightened fire risks at full charge

items.summary: Lithium-ion batteries charged to full capacity were far more likely to catch fire or undergo thermal runaway when subjected to external pressure, according to tests released by Seoul on Monday, raising questions about safety practices in warehouses storing large quantities of batteries. The Seoul Metropolitan Fire and Disaster Headquarters said four out of five batteries in both cylindrical and pouch-shaped categories experienced thermal runaway and ignition when charged to 100 percent. The tests were conducted by the headquarters’ Fire Investigation Research Center following a July fire at a logistics center in Incheon, as authorities examined whether battery charge levels should be regulated during distribution and storage. Researchers tested two commercially available types — cylindrical 18650 lithium-ion batteries and pouch-shaped lithium-ion polymer batteries — at charge levels of 30 percent, 50 percent, 70 percent and 100 percent. items.title: Murder of runaway teen exposes gaps in protection system

items.summary: The murder of a 15-year-old girl in Seoul's Seongbuk District has drawn attention to the dangers posed by adults who approach runaway teenagers with promises of food and shelter but may exploit them for criminal purposes. The case has also raised concerns about gaps in Korea's protection system for young people living away from home amid allegations that the victim, who had been moving between youth shelters, was coerced into prostitution and other criminal activities. According to police and other authorities Sunday, a 59-year-old man surnamed Jin, who was arrested on suspicion of killing the girl at a shared accommodation facility in Jeongneung-dong, Seongbuk District, was formally detained Friday and remains under police investigation. The Seoul Northern District Court issued an arrest warrant for Jin, citing concerns that he might destroy evidence or flee. Jin has reportedly been uncooperative with investigators, including refusing to answer questions. items.title: King Salman orders promotion and appointment of 167 judges at Justice Ministry
items.title_zh: 萨勒曼国王下令晋升和任命司法部167名法官
items.summary: RIYADH — Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman has issued a royal order promoting and appointing 167 judges at the Ministry of Justice across various ranks.Minister of Justice and Acting President of the Supreme Judicial Council Walid Al-Samaani said that the order reflects the King’s continued support for the judicial sector, along with the follow-up and backing of Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman and their commitment to raising its efficiency and improving its outcomes.He noted that the promotions and appointments will contribute to the development of the sector, enhance judicial performance, and improve the quality of rulings, in line with the ongoing advancement of the justice system. Al-Samaani expressed his gratitude to the Kingdom’s leadership for its support of the judicial sector, praying for the judges’ success in carrying out their duties and upholding justice.

items.summary: RIYADH — Two drones, launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Makkah region, were intercepted and destroyed. This was disclosed by Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen. Another drone was intercepted and destroyed in the Madinah region, he added.

items.title: Safety bracelet service enhances care for children and elderly at Makkah Grand Mosque
items.title_zh: 安全手环服务加强了对麦加禁寺内儿童和老年人的关照
items.summary: MAKKAH — The General Authority for the Care of the Affairs of the Grand Mosque and the Prophet’s Mosque is providing safety bracelets to visitors of the Grand Mosque to facilitate the identification and location of children, elderly people and persons with disabilities if they become separated from their companions. The initiative aims to enhance visitor safety and ensure their well-being while they are inside the Grand Mosque and its courtyards. The service is provided free of charge through the guest care centers. Beneficiaries are given bracelets containing identification details, which enable staff on the ground to identify them and contact their families when necessary. This initiative reflects the authority’s commitment to prioritizing safety and humanitarian care, ensuring a secure and accessible environment for all who visit the Grand Mosque, thereby facilitating their journey and allowing them to perform their worship with peace of mind.

items.title: Commerce ministry recalls 2,214 Bose speakers over battery overheating and fire risk
items.title_zh: 商务部召回2214只Bose音箱，原因是电池过热和存在火灾风险
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Commerce announced the recall of 2,214 Bose speakers, models S1 Pro+ and S1 Pro, due to the possibility of the batteries overheating during use, which could pose a fire hazard. The ministry urged users of the affected products to stop using them immediately and contact aDawliah Electronic Appliances Company on (01126669932) to have the battery replaced free of charge. Users can check whether their products are included in the recall campaign through the website of the Defective Products Recall Center: http://Recalls.sa.

items.title: Inflation in Saudi Arabia reaches 1.7% in October
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯10月份的通胀率达到1.7%
items.summary: RIYADH — Inflation or Consumer Price Index (CPI) in Saudi Arabia registered an annual increase of 1.7 percent in October 2026 compared to the same month last year, according to data released on Sunday by the General Authority for Statistics (GASTAT). The authority attributed the rise primarily to a 3.5 percent increase in housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuel prices, alongside a 1.1 percent rise in food and beverage prices and a 2.3 percent increase in transportation prices.In terms of consumer spending, the report revealed that actual housing rents increased by 3.5 percent, while prices in insurance and financial services also rose by 3.5 percent, driven by a 6.5 percent increase in insurance service prices.Prices in the recreation, sports and culture sector climbed by 2.7 percent, reflecting a 4.6 percent increase in holiday package prices. Passenger transportation services recorded a more substantial rise of 9.5 percent. Conversely, prices in the furniture, household appliances and routine home maintenance category declined by 0.5 percent while those in the clothing and footwear category fell by 0.2 percent.The housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels category emerged as the largest contributor to the annual inflation rate, accounting for 0.7 percentage points. This was followed by transportation at 0.3 percentage points, food and beverages at 0.2 percentage points, and personal care, social protection and other goods and services at 0.1 percentage points. The remaining categories collectively contributed 0.4 percentage points.On a month-on-month basis, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased by 0.1 percent in October compared to September 2026. The rise was driven by a 0.2 percent increase in housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuel prices, supported by a 0.4 percent rise in actual housing rents. Food and beverage prices also increased by 0.2 percent, while insurance and financial services rose by 1.5 percent, recreation, sports and culture by 0.2 percent, clothing and footwear by 0.4 percent, and health by 0.2 percent.Conversely, prices in personal care, social protection and other goods and services declined by 0.6 percent. Prices remained unchanged in transportation, restaurants and accommodation services, furniture, household appliances and routine home maintenance, education services, and tobacco.The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in the Kingdom recorded an annual increase of 4.5 percent in October 2026 compared to the same month in 2025, according to GASTAT report. The increase was primarily driven by higher prices of other transportable goods, excluding metal products and machinery, as well as food, beverages, tobacco and textiles.Prices of other transportable goods rose by 8 percent, reflecting a 24.2 percent increase in basic chemical prices and a 5.5 percent rise in refined petroleum products and fuels.Meanwhile, prices of food, beverages, tobacco and textiles increased by 1.6 percent, driven by a 2.6 percent rise in the prices of meat, fish, fruits, vegetables and oils, alongside a 1 percent increase in grain mill products, starches and other food products.Prices of agricultural and fishing products climbed by 4.1 percent, supported by increases of 4.7 percent in agricultural product prices and 3.3 percent in live animals and animal products. Prices of ores and minerals also rose by 2 percent, reflecting an equivalent increase in the prices of stones and sand. In contrast, prices of metal products, machinery and equipment declined by 0.3 percent, mainly due to a 3.5 percent decrease in basic metal prices.On a monthly basis, the Wholesale Price Index increased by 1.1 percent in October compared to September 2026. The increase was primarily driven by a 1.9 percent rise in the prices of other transportable goods, underpinned by a 3.1percent increase in basic chemical prices and a 2.8 percent rise in refined petroleum products and fuels.Prices of agricultural and fishing products also increased by 0.6 percent, while food, beverages, tobacco and textiles recorded a 0.2 percent rise. Conversely, prices of ores and minerals declined by 0.2 percent, while those of metal products, machinery and equipment remained virtually unchanged.

items.title: Municipalities ministry issues 80,775 building permits across Saudi Arabia in 9 months
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯市政部在9个月内发放了80,775份建筑许可证
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Municipalities and Housing has issued 80,775 building permits across Saudi Arabia from January through the end of September 2026. This is part of the ministry's efforts to regulate construction activities, streamline building permit procedures, and keep pace with urban growth in cities and governorates. The ministry said that improving licensing services is part of its efforts to enhance the efficiency of city operations, improve the urban environment, and facilitate access to municipal services for individuals and investors, thereby enhancing the quality of the urban experience and supporting the development of more efficient cities that better meet residents' needs. The ministry noted that streamlining procedures and improving the efficiency of digital services support urban development and investment activity, improve the quality of projects within cities, and align with the ministry's objectives of improving quality of life, enhancing service quality, and improving the urban landscape.

items.title: Riyadh begins construction of 70,000-square-meter Expo 2030 Metro station
items.title_zh: 利雅得开始建设7万平方米的2030年世博会地铁站
items.summary: RIYADH — The Royal Commission for Riyadh City (RCRC) has started construction work on the Riyadh Metro’s “Expo” station, which will cover approximately 70,000 square meters and accommodate up to 19,000 passengers per hour, alongside the unveiling of its architectural design. The project forms part of the commission’s efforts to develop the capital’s transportation network and keep pace with its population, urban and economic growth. The station will facilitate access for Expo visitors through the public transportation system and serve as a permanent addition to the Riyadh Metro network while continuing to serve the surrounding area and nearby destinations after the exhibition concludes. Located on the Riyadh Metro’s Yellow Line, which connects to King Khalid International Airport, the station will extend over King Salman Road within a green corridor linking the Expo 2030 Riyadh site to the east with future urban development areas to the west. Its architectural design draws inspiration from Riyadh’s natural landscape, particularly its valleys and acacia trees. The station will feature a steel dome measuring 134 meters in diameter, supported by eight branching columns resembling acacia trees and providing shaded spaces for visitors. It will also include approximately 44,000 square meters of green spaces, alongside solar energy systems designed to cover around 25 percent of its energy consumption. The commission is implementing the project according to a schedule coordinated with the development of the Expo site, ensuring its completion alongside the site's readiness and before the exhibition begins. Construction will follow a traffic management plan developed in coordination with relevant authorities, including alternative routes to minimize disruption to traffic and surrounding residential neighborhoods while maintaining smooth traffic flow and access to the area throughout the construction period.

items.title: Southern Armed Forces announce redeployment from Bab al-Mandab to bolster Aden’s defenses
items.title_zh: 南方武装部队宣布从曼德海峡重新部署，以加强亚丁的防御
items.summary: ADEN — Yemen’s Southern Armed Forces announced on Sunday the redeployment of their forces from districts and the Bab Al-Mandab area, west of Taiz Governorate, as part of efforts to strengthen military positions and prioritize the security of Aden and neighboring governorates. In a statement issued on Sunday, the forces said the move follows recent developments on the battlefronts, including military buildups and threats targeting Aden and its surrounding area, as well as reports of hostile armed groups moving through areas overlooking the city. The redeployment aims to reorganize military positions, reinforce key fronts and strengthen the forces’ presence in areas and along routes required by the current circumstances. The Southern Armed Forces stressed that securing Aden and neighboring governorates remains a priority, alongside confronting existing threats and continuing military operations against the Houthi militia. They reaffirmed that their confrontation with the Houthis would continue until the Houthi rebellion ends, state institutions are restored, and security and stability are achieved. The forces also emphasized their commitment to maintaining security and stability in Aden and eliminating Houthi threats to the city, with the support and assistance of the Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen, led by Saudi Arabia. The statement further stressed that national duty and shared responsibility in confronting threats are not confined to any particular geographical location, but are determined by operational requirements and the public interest. The Southern Armed Forces praised the efforts and sacrifices of their personnel across various battlefronts, describing them as a source of pride and appreciation. They renewed their commitment to protecting their people’s security and stability, emphasizing that changing circumstances and developments on the ground would not deter them from fulfilling their national duties and responsibilities.

items.title: Saudi Arabia condemns Iranian aerial attacks on Bahrain, calls for immediate halt
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯谴责伊朗对巴林的空袭，呼吁立即停止
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia has strongly condemned the Iranian aerial attacks on Bahrain, following a claim by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) that it had launched six drones targeting a US radar system in the Kingdom. In a statement issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Sunday, Saudi Arabia reaffirmed its full solidarity with Bahrain in all measures taken to safeguard its security and stability. It also stressed that the Iranian attacks constitute a violation of international law and the principles of good neighborliness. The Kingdom emphasized the importance of immediately halting of blatant Iranian attacks on countries in the region. The statement concluded with Saudi Arabia calling for serious steps toward achieving security and stability for the countries and peoples of the region.

items.title: Saudi air defenses intercept 2 ballistic missiles, drone targeting Riyadh and Eastern regions
items.title_zh: 沙特防空部队拦截了两枚弹道导弹和一架无人机，后者瞄准了利雅得和东部地区
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles and a drone launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Riyadh and Eastern regions on Sunday morning. Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen spokesperson Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki announced early Sunday that air defenses had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles targeting the Riyadh region. A few hours later, Al-Maliki announced that coalition forces had intercepted and destroyed a drone launched toward the Eastern Province.
